title: NIST: standard atomic weight of Barium (Ba, Z=56) is 137.327(7)
summary: NIST prints the standard atomic weight field of Barium (Ba, Z=56) as 137.327(7), with the isotope rows in the same file.
body: PubChem's periodic-table row names atomic number 56, symbol Ba, as Barium. The NIST compositions file prints the standard atomic weight of Barium as 137.327(7). The parenthesis is the uncertainty NIST prints on the last digits of that standard atomic weight. It is an evaluated standard, not one laboratory weighing of one sample. The notes field on this element's rows is blank. Isotope rows in the same file: Ba-130 relative atomic mass 129.9063207(28), isotopic composition 0.00106(1); Ba-132 relative atomic mass 131.9050611(11), isotopic composition 0.00101(1); Ba-134 relative atomic mass 133.90450818(30), isotopic composition 0.02417(18); Ba-135 relative atomic mass 134.90568838(29), isotopic composition 0.06592(12); Ba-136 relative atomic mass 135.90457573(29), isotopic composition 0.07854(24); Ba-137 relative atomic mass 136.90582714(30), isotopic composition 0.11232(24); Ba-138 relative atomic mass 137.90524700(31), isotopic composition 0.71698(42). A relative atomic mass is scaled to carbon-12. An isotopic composition, when the field is not blank, is a representative mole fraction, not a new assay made for this card. The symbols for an interval, a parenthesis, a bracket, and a # mark are defined on world.chemistry.nist-atomic-weight-notation. This standard atomic weight is not the Chemistry WebBook molecular-weight field, which is a different catalog entry when one exists.
